summary: NO spec attribute is added, removed or renamed. Two VALIDATION-BEHAVIOUR changes only: (1) V-CYC-7 (reconciliation source must have an append-only producer) is narrowed from both pipeline modes to execution_mode 'pipeline' alone, because 'pipeline_audit_only' reads its source as a batch and registers no heal lane -- the mode the guard's own message, docs/07 section 11.7 and docs/13 R7 have always named as the fix was itself rejected, leaving a MERGE-written source with no legal in-pipeline setting at all; (2) the onboarding preflight's append_schema check stops comparing source columns against append_target_table when the flow declares transform_sql, reporting the new advisory status SHAPE_DEFINED_BY_TRANSFORM_SQL instead of a false SCHEMA_MISMATCH. Both are relaxations: every spec that validated before still validates, and no onboarded control-table row changes shape.

modified_attributes.what_changed: VALIDATION ONLY -- the field, its enum, its default and its control-table column are all unchanged. What changed is which values V-CYC-7 applies to. Through v1.7.10 a reconciliation flow whose source_config.table resolved to an in-spec target produced by SCD1/SCD2/SCD3/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC (or TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD into a materialized_view) was REJECTED under BOTH 'pipeline' and 'pipeline_audit_only'. From v1.7.11 it is rejected under 'pipeline' only.
modified_attributes.why_it_changed: The rule existed because execution_mode 'pipeline' STREAMS the reconciliation source: reconciliation/graph_registration.py binds the L3 _src node and the L5 heal pulse with want_stream=needs_heal, and needs_heal is only ever true under 'pipeline'. A Delta stream cannot read a MERGE-written table (DELTA_SOURCE_TABLE_IGNORE_CHANGES), and skipChangeCommits is refused framework-wide. 'pipeline_audit_only' binds the same node with want_stream=False -- a batch dlt.read -- and returns before registering any heal lane, so the hazard does not exist for it. The framework already said so in three places (engine/source_plane.py's G-STREAM message, docs/07 section 11.7, docs/13 R7) while the validator contradicted all three.
modified_attributes.user_visible_effect: A spec that was previously rejected now onboards. Nothing that previously onboarded is now rejected.
modified_attributes.rejection_message_verbatim_pipeline_mode: reconciliation_flow[<id>].source_config.table: is produced by cdc_load_strategy 'SCD1', which dispatches through dlt.apply_changes[_from_snapshot] (real MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE writes, not append-only) -- execution_mode 'pipeline' streams this source for the L5 heal pulse, so it requires an append-only producer. Set execution_mode to 'pipeline_audit_only' (the comparison stays in this pipeline as a batch read; healing moves to the 05_reconciliation_engine.py job task) or to 'job' to keep the standalone engine for this source.

reconciliation_flow[<id>].source_config.table: is produced by cdc_load_strategy 'TRUNCATE_AND_LOAD' into target_type 'materialized_view', which is fully refreshed (not append-only) on every update -- execution_mode 'pipeline' streams this source for the L5 heal pulse, so it requires an append-only producer. Set execution_mode to 'pipeline_audit_only' (the comparison stays in this pipeline as a batch read; healing moves to the 05_reconciliation_engine.py job task) or to 'job' to keep the standalone engine for this source.
modified_attributes.migration: None. No spec edit is required by this change. Authors who worked around the old behaviour by setting execution_mode 'job' MAY now move to 'pipeline_audit_only' to get the comparison, __metrics and dq_config expectations inside the pipeline update; if they do, they must add the matching 05_reconciliation_engine.py job task per reconciliation_id, because audit-only does not heal.
modified_attributes.ui_action: Text only -- no widget, option or visibility rule changes. In the reconciliation execution_mode help text, the sentence 'Both pipeline modes require dataflow_group_id, an append-only source producer, and read_mode batch on every side' is now WRONG and must be corrected to: 'Both pipeline modes require dataflow_group_id and read_mode batch on every side. Only pipeline additionally requires an append-only source producer, because it streams the source to drive the heal lane; pipeline_audit_only reads the source as a batch and is the correct mode when the source is written by SCD1/SCD2/SCD3/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC or is a fully refreshed materialized view.' Apply the identical correction everywhere that sentence is duplicated.
modified_attributes.validation: No new rule. spec_validator.py::_validate_reconciliation_pipeline_placement now gates the V-CYC-7 block on `execution_mode == "pipeline"` instead of the `pipeline_mode` boolean. Every other V-CYC rule keeps its existing mode scoping: V-CYC-1 and V-CYC-6 stay on both pipeline modes, and the append-loop rules (V-CYC-2/3/5) stay error-in-pipeline-modes / warning-in-job.

modified_attributes.what_changed: VALIDATION ONLY -- the field is unchanged and still validated for parse-ability via the EXPLAIN-based check. What changed is the onboarding PREFLIGHT report (onboarding/uc_spec_preflight.py, the preflight_check_onboarding_spec UC function): when a reconciliation flow declares a non-blank transform_sql, the 'append_schema' existence check no longer compares the SOURCE table's columns against append_target_table's columns.
modified_attributes.why_it_changed: The check assumed the appended rows carry the source table's own columns. That is only true when transform_sql is absent. reconciliation/appender.py::apply_transform_sql runs the SQL over the miss set BEFORE append_missing_records writes it, so with transform_sql the appended shape is that SQL's SELECT list. The old check therefore reported SCHEMA_MISMATCH for every correctly written reshaping flow -- UC3's batch lane reshapes a 31/90/131-column staging row into the 9-column Debezium landing row, which would have been flagged as missing every business column.
modified_attributes.new_status_note_verbatim: append_target_table of reconciliation_flow[<flow_id>].target_configs[<target_id>] receives rows reshaped by this flow's transform_sql, so the appended shape is that SQL's SELECT list rather than the source table's columns and cannot be compared statically here -- verify the SELECT list against the table's columns yourself (the append runs with mergeSchema, so a misspelt alias ADDS a column rather than failing)
modified_attributes.user_visible_effect: An existence_checks entry of kind 'append_schema' may now carry status 'SHAPE_DEFINED_BY_TRANSFORM_SQL'. It is advisory and never affects `valid` (only MISSING_REQUIRED does). Flows WITHOUT transform_sql still get SCHEMA_OK / SCHEMA_MISMATCH exactly as before.
modified_attributes.ui_action: Any consumer that renders or switches on existence_checks[].status must tolerate the new value. Render it as informational (not an error, not a success) -- the same weight as a note. No other change.
modified_attributes.validation: No spec-level rule added or removed; the preflight report is advisory by contract.

required: config/registry/reconciliation.json: correct the execution_mode description sentence (see modified_attributes[0].ui_action).
web/src/registry.js: same sentence; then `npm run build` in databricks-app/web, because Databricks Apps does not build at deploy time.
Any status-rendering code path: accept SHAPE_DEFINED_BY_TRANSFORM_SQL.
server/settings.py: no change expected -- confirm, do not assume.
config/validation/rules.json: no change -- the app's bp_* rules do not encode V-CYC-7.
